sources.title: Charles Holcombe, The Sixteen Kingdoms, Cambridge History of China (2019), chapter summary
sources.note: Publisher chapter summary checked, not the paywalled chapter. Gives 304 to 439, up to 22 significant states, multiethnic conquest empires and governors claiming Jin allegiance.

sources.title: Palace Museum: Sixteen Kingdoms chronology and constituent states
sources.note: Indexed original Chinese entry checked; direct fetch failed. Dates Liu Yuan proclaiming himself king of Han in 304 and Northern Wei unification in 439; enumerates the conventional sixteen states.

sources.title: Bagongshan District government: Battle of the Fei River
sources.note: Direct Chinese heritage account read. Used only for Fu Jian, Former Qin, Eastern Jin and defeat in 383; legendary dialogue and large troop/casualty totals omitted.

sources.title: Asian Art Museum: Buddha dated 338, B60B1034
sources.note: Direct museum essay and inscription transcription checked. Original sample is the first four Chinese characters, with museum translation. Technical claims from How Was It Made?; holes and proposed missing attachments from Imagining the Original. Same-object catalogue treated as one work, not a second word allowance.

sources.title: Nicholas Sims-Williams and Daniel Waugh: Sogdian Ancient Letters 1, 2, 3 and 5
sources.note: University of Washington edition directly read. Date 313 to 314 is the editors’ preferred dating. Personal narrative from Letters 1 and 3; merchant goods from introduction and Letter 5; news about Luoyang from Letter 2. These are regional contemporary witnesses, not official voices of a unified state.

sources.title: CNR: First discovery of sacrificial traces and grain in Shaanxi Sixteen Kingdoms tombs (11 January 2019)
sources.note: Indexed original report checked, quoting excavation director Liu Daiyun of the Shaanxi archaeological institute; subsequent direct fetch failed. Twelve tombs in two rows; household models; piglet skulls and millet under a stone; military seals. Kinship is an archaeological interpretation, not a completed DNA result.

sources.title: Shandong University archaeology: Xie Gaowen on Xianyang Sixteen Kingdoms tombs (26 November 2025)
sources.note: Direct university report of the excavator’s lecture read. Specific witnesses are Pingling M1 female musicians, planned family cemeteries and Wenlin M49 dated brick. Translates instruments conservatively; does not turn burial figures into population statistics.

sources.title: Tongwancheng National Archaeological Site Park: site introduction
sources.note: Direct site description checked: Helian Bobo’s Xia capital, west and east inner cities, outer city, palace area, towers, projecting defenses and moat. No claim of UNESCO World Heritage inscription.

sources.title: Weng, Zhang and Li: Analysis of Construction Materials of Xiongnu Tongwan City (Studies in Conservation 66, 2021)
sources.note: Complete publisher abstract checked in indexed original; direct fetch failed. West-city samples contain lime, sand and clay, protein components and peach gum detected by immunoassay. Whiteness is a proposed combination of factors, not a proven single recipe. Full article was not accessed.

sources.title: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Renditions: Kumarajiva biography
sources.note: Complete indexed university biography checked; direct extraction exposes only heading. Uses 401 arrival and Later Qin ruler Yao Xing, captivity and influence of translations. Avoids the source’s questionable 382 invasion date and uncertain birth/death years.

proposedOverrides.name: Sixteen Kingdoms
proposedOverrides.summary: Competing northern Chinese states connected by warfare, migration, trade and Buddhist learning.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Distinct collective period card, not an alias for Eastern Jin or Northern Wei.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: Public overview flags collective outline, geometry surviving to 500 and omission of western communities. Dunhuang letter evidence comes from the period’s broader western networks; no claim that Dunhuang lies inside the polygon. Historical interval preserved from current index. Periods are selected interpretive phases, with exclusive boundaries.
